items.message: Prompt text from bound adapters flows into `difflib.unified_diff` and then into `click.echo` without sanitization. A malicious lockstep.py (or a house prompt body file) can inject terminal escape sequences — including OSC 8 hyperlinks, cursor repositioning, or color codes — into the diff output, which some terminals interpret and execute. The error message in `_resolve_prompt` echoes the user-supplied `name` argument directly into a `ClickException` message via an f-string (`f"{name!r} is ambiguous"`). The `!r` repr quoting limits injection into surrounding prose, but the raw value also appears in the second branch (`f"no prompt named {name!r}"`). `_bound_compositions` iterates `lockstep.container.resolved()` and calls `.compositions()` on every instance satisfying `Inspectable`. If a third-party adapter's `compositions()` raises or returns a malformed dict, the exception propagates unhandled to the CLI. More concretely, if `compositions()` returns a `Composition` whose `prompt.system(layers)` performs file I/O (reading an arbitrary path via `Body.from_path`), calling `.text()` later in `show-prompt` reads that path.
